status_note: Live and battle-tested: this exact image runs in a production AWS Nitro enclave guarding real Telegram accounts. Not a development, staging, or testnet build. The release is commit-pinned and reproducible; trust comes from rebuilding it and matching the PCR0 below, plus the live in-browser attestation.
gateway_commit_repo: github.com/Danimal01/enclave-gateway (THIS repository) — resolve gateway_commit/the tag here, not elsewhere; tag v1.0.11 is the source that builds to pcr0_g.
allowlist_sha256_preimage: IMPORTANT: allowlist_sha256 is INTENTIONALLY DIFFERENT from files[].sha256 below and is NOT supposed to equal it (this is not a mismatch). allowlist_sha256 = sha256 over the UTF-8 string '// FILE tg-chokepoint.mjs\n' concatenated with the file's bytes -- the attestation-binding digest the live attestation binds and the how-it-works page verifies. files[].sha256 = the plain `sha256sum tg-chokepoint.mjs`. Two verifiers, two values, same file.

files.name: tg-chokepoint.mjs
files.note: raw sha256 of the file bytes; matches `sha256sum tg-chokepoint.mjs`. Intentionally DIFFERS from the top-level allowlist_sha256 (the attestation-binding digest) -- see allowlist_sha256_preimage.

reproducible_note: umask-independent: a 644 and a 664 source context build the IDENTICAL PCR0 (the Dockerfile canonicalizes every COPYed file's mode; .gitattributes pins LF). The OS toolchain is pinned to a frozen Amazon Linux 2023 snapshot (dnf --releasever=2023.12.20260608) so the compiled native modules and attest binary stay byte-deterministic and the PCR0 does not drift as AL's rolling repo moves. The three host-staged binaries above are pinned by sha256 so a verifier can confirm them. Build on any host and match.
transparency: To verify: check out tag v1.0.11 of THIS repository, rebuild per BUILD.md, and confirm the PCR0 matches pcr0_g. The tag is the exact source that builds to pcr0_g.

attestation.note: A live AWS Nitro enclave running this exact image attests PCR0_G above (the live artifact is authoritative for the current module id and timestamp). The capability allowlist (tg-chokepoint.mjs) is account-management only: no message, chat, file, or contact method. The one call whose reply can carry message updates, updates.getDifference, is read single-branch (only otherUpdates) and its newMessages are discarded unread.

note: Production release v1.0.11: adds tdata-replay (session-clone) detection and revocation. A copied Telegram Desktop session (the tdata folder) reuses the victim's existing auth_key, so a hijacked desktop appears as the SAME already-whitelisted session with NO new-login push -- invisible to Telegram's own device list and to any new-device check. The gateway classifies a whitelisted session that shows impossible movement -- a country FLAP (oscillation between countries) or a TELEPORT to a locality outside its learned baseline -- as a contested replay, and under the SIGNED auto_burn contest-protection policy revokes the shared session via account.resetAuthorization. Detection rides the existing account.getAuthorizations roster diff at an adaptive cadence (~2s baseline, ~1s hot-watch once a teleport is seen) with a high-confidence first-poll burn when the move is cross-country AND the device changed, so a clone is evicted in about a second, before it can read or act. Because a tdata copy shares the ONE auth_key, revoking it signs the victim's own desktop out too; they sign back in and the copy cannot follow (it lacks the phone). The contested 'sign back in' banner auto-clears once the user's own device reconnects (a whitelisted session created after the burn), published authoritatively by the enclave so a stale row cannot linger. CAPABILITY-NEUTRAL: tg-chokepoint.mjs is BYTE-IDENTICAL -- the burn reuses account.resetAuthorization and account.getAuthorizations, both already in the allowlist -- so allowlist_sha256 and files[] are UNCHANGED from v1.0.10; only enclave logic changed, hence a new PCR0 (8bd012fe). The contest-protection ENABLE is sourced ONLY from the signed M-of-N policy chain (deriveAuthority): a whitelisted hash is burned iff the signed contest_protection is exactly auto_burn AND the brain requested the override for that op (a compromised brain cannot burn a kept session). Known limitation, addressed in v1.0.12: for an account with 2FA OFF a contested burn currently degrades to alert-only; it will fire regardless next, since for a copied-session attack the revoke is protective without 2FA (the attacker holds a dead session copy, not the phone). Carries forward v1.0.10 (PCR0 724a471e): fixes a benign activity-log false-positive where the guard logged its OWN session as a 'New login from an unknown device'. On reconnect Telegram replays the guard's own login as an UpdateNewAuthorization carrying the session's REAL non-zero hash, while account.getAuthorizations reports our own session as current with hash 0 -- so the gateway's fail-open detector could not match the push to our self row and recorded a scary false alarm. v1.0.10 restores the prior worker generation's park-and-match: a new-login push is PARKED and only written to the activity log once a getAuthorizations sweep confirms that hash as a real session (current:false, non-whitelisted), tagged with its real device. Our own session is current and never appears as a non-current row, so the self-replay is NEVER logged; a genuine intruder IS logged -- including one detected during the adoption window (the resolver runs on the seed sweep) or evicted in the same sweep (the resolver matches the pre-eviction listed roster). Eviction/protection is entirely roster-driven and gated on !current, so it is untouched; detection still has two independent surfaces (the push-triggered sweep and the ~7s roster diff). The only un-logged case is a session that vanishes before any roster read can observe it -- information-theoretically indistinguishable from our own echo and not a persistent threat. CAPABILITY-NEUTRAL: tg-chokepoint.mjs is BYTE-IDENTICAL, so allowlist_sha256 and files[].sha256 are UNCHANGED from v1.0.9 -- only enclave logic changed, hence a new PCR0 (724a471e). Validated by a multi-agent red team (including an information-theoretic indistinguishability proof and an independent diff review) and 53 passing gateway unit tests. Carries forward v1.0.9 (PCR0 6522a6e0): propagates post-arm signed policy changes into the running enclave. The State Authority policy head was only ever set to v1 at arm and never advanced (compare_and_advance was deployed but never called), so the enclave anchored its authority to v1 and silently ignored every post-arm signed change -- allow-reset (turn off 2FA-reset protection), set-whitelist (edit the keep-list), set-threshold, add-key, remove-key. Only disconnect propagated (it has its own independent re-verify path). v1.0.9 adds a reconcilePolicy pass (cloned from that proven disconnect path) that runs each sweep, after disconnect-reconcile and before the eviction sweep: a cheap pre-check, then under the per-account lock a single full-chain deriveAuthority anchored at the verified head, a fenced compare_and_advance walking the State Authority head forward one version at a time, and a lockstep refresh of the enforced authority. Fail-safe: a forged/unsigned row anywhere -> no State Authority write, authority untouched; any transient error -> keep last-good, retry next sweep; every CAS carries the live lease holder/epoch fence. CAPABILITY-NEUTRAL: tg-chokepoint.mjs is BYTE-IDENTICAL, so allowlist_sha256 and files[].sha256 are UNCHANGED from v1.0.8 -- only the enclave logic changed, hence a new PCR0 (6522a6e0). Existing armed accounts auto-backfill from v1 to their true signed head on the first post-cutover sweep (validated live: an account at chain head v5 advanced v1->v5 in DynamoDB immediately after cutover). 15 added unit tests + independent review; reproducible double-build; KMS append-only re-pin keeping v1.0.8 (18f0f9a3) pinned for rollback. Carries forward v1.0.8 (PCR0 18f0f9a3), build-determinism hardening that pins the dnf toolchain to a frozen Amazon Linux 2023 snapshot (--releasever=2023.12.20260608). Carries forward v1.0.7: fixes an eviction-LOGGING loop with NO capability change (allowlist_sha256 and files[].sha256 are byte-identical to v1.0.6). After a successful account.resetAuthorization, Telegram can keep LISTING the terminated session as a ghost in account.getAuthorizations for minutes; the detection sweep recomputed its target set from the live roster each cycle with no memory, so it re-removed + re-logged + re-emailed the same already-killed session every ~7s until Telegram GCs it. The gateway now dedups against the durable eviction_log keyed on the per-session hash: a hash removed within a 30-min cooldown is not re-proposed (a real new login always carries a NEW hash, so a genuine intruder is never suppressed), a cooled-still-listed ghost is excluded from the roster baseline so it is never misreported as a new login or a sign-out-elsewhere, and a session that genuinely persists past the window falls back into the normal gated batch and is surfaced to the operator. Carries forward v1.0.6 reliable instant new-login detection (updates.getDifference state machine), v1.0.5 activity-log accuracy, v1.0.4 warmth, v1.0.3 SRP, v1.0.2 disconnect-execution. Deterministic, umask-independent reproducibility.
